flockdeck — runs your coding agents on hardware you control.

Usage:
  flockdeck [flags]

Flags:
  -C directory
    	directory to open the workspace on
    	(default: $FLOCKDECK_DIR if set, else the working directory) (default ".")
  -agent id
    	id of the agent new panes start as for this run; flockdeck agents lists them
    	(default: $FLOCKDECK_START_AGENT if set)
  -detach
    	keep running without a window; reattach later by running it again
    	(default: $FLOCKDECK_DETACH if set to 1 or true)
  -new
    	ignore any saved layout and start with a single pane
    	(default: $FLOCKDECK_FRESH if set to 1 or true)
  -no-window
    	do not open a window or need a browser here; print the URL and keep serving
    	(default: $FLOCKDECK_NO_WINDOW if set to 1 or true)
  -quit
    	stop a running instance and its agents
  -shell
    	open the first pane as a shell instead of an agent
    	(default: $FLOCKDECK_SHELL_FIRST if set to 1 or true)
  -solo
    	always start a new instance instead of attaching to a running one
    	(default: $FLOCKDECK_SOLO if set to 1 or true)
  -version
    	print the version and exit

Subcommands:
  spawn [--worktree <branch>] [--split] [--shell] [--agent <id>] [--model <model>] <task>
        start another agent; run from inside a pane
        run flockdeck spawn -h for what the flags do
  peer-name <name>
        report the name another Claude session would address this pane by; run from inside a pane
  close [-force] <pane-id> | close -finished
        close another pane, or every finished one; run from inside a pane
  agents
        list the agents flockdeck can run, with their models
  chat [flags]
        flockdeck's own chat client, which an API agent's pane runs; chat -h for its flags
  keys [list|set <agent>|clear <agent>|check <agent>|endpoint <agent> [<url> | default]]
        the API keys agents talk to a model API with
  remote enable [-relay <url>] [-name <name>] [-join <code>] [-invite <code>]
        enrol this machine with a relay, so another device can reach its agents
  remote pair [-desktop] | status | devices | revoke <id> | disable [-force]
        pair a device, and see or change what is paired
  remote rename [-device <id or name>] <name>
        rename this machine, or a paired device, as every device lists it
  remote move [-invite <code>] [-join <code>] [-name <name>] [-yes] <relay>
        move this machine to another relay; every device then pairs again
  update [-check]
        fetch the latest release and put it in place
  help [<subcommand>]
        this usage, or a subcommand's own

Environment:
  FLOCKDECK_UPDATE=off
        do not look for new releases in the background; update still works
  FLOCKDECK_RELAY=<url>
        the relay remote access goes through, instead of the default one
  FLOCKDECK_API_KEY=<key>
        the key any API agent uses when neither its own variables nor a key
        stored with `flockdeck keys set` hold one
  FLOCKDECK_DIR=<directory>, FLOCKDECK_START_AGENT=<id>, FLOCKDECK_RELAY=<url>
  FLOCKDECK_FRESH / FLOCKDECK_SHELL_FIRST / FLOCKDECK_NO_WINDOW / FLOCKDECK_DETACH / FLOCKDECK_SOLO=1
        the environment equivalents of -C, -agent, -relay, -new, -shell,
        -no-window, -detach and -solo, for a systemd unit or container manifest;
        a flag given on the command line always wins

Running it again attaches to an instance that is already going.
Press F1 in the window for the help: the shortcuts, and how the rest of it works.
